title: Positive Chern and section-one normalization
statement: Let Ω be an algebraically closed field, N>0 invertible in Ω, A a finite commutative ring with N=0 in A, S=Spec Ω, P=P¹_S, X=D(x₀)=A¹_S, and k=[1:0]. Fix any boundary/counit data d satisfying [lem-pur-origin-boundary-counit-data], using the arrows of [def-pur-origin-comparison-arrows]. The dual of the point ideal is isomorphic to O_P(1), and has the positive transition frames of [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. There exist an ordinary finite Chern arrow c:A_P→L_P[2] satisfying ordinaryFiniteP1ChernSpec (the positive Kummer class of O(1)), and an isomorphism λ:A[0]≅RΓ(P,j_!i_*A). With u:A_P→k_*A the specified supportedConstantUnit, η:A[0]→RΓ(P,A_P) the specified originConstantSectionsUnit, bP the fixed d.projectiveClass arrow and e the fixed d support counit, they satisfy u ≫ bP = c and λ.hom ≫ RΓ(e) = η ≫ RΓ(u). No boundary/counit data is constructed and no final compact-image equality is assumed.

proof.text: On the chart D(x0), the ideal of [1:0] is generated by t=x1/x0; on D(x1) it is generated by 1. Both are Cartier frames. Their dual frames have transition g0=t^(-1)g1, exactly the positive twist convention. Glue the frame identifications with O(1), and retain them as TwistData. The divisor section has coordinates t,1 and is x1.

proof.text: Define c by Yoneda precomposition of the fixed projective boundary with the supported constant unit. The degree-zero Ext realization gives u ≫ bP = c. Exact coefficient forgetting and the supported coefficient-unit identity identify the resulting ordinary finite class with the Kummer class of the dual divisor ideal; the isomorphism from the first step identifies this with the positive O(1) class. This proves ordinaryFiniteP1ChernSpec, including its sign.

proof.text: Use compact-point-source normalization for the closed rational point in P1. Finite exact pushforward, derived sections composition, and the equivalence of the etale topos of an algebraically closed point with sets show the constant-section/closed-unit composite θ=η ≫ RΓ(u) is invertible and sends one to one. Match its canonical constant-pullback comparisons with supportedConstantUnit: their difference is a sheaf automorphism. Match the localized constant/global-sections adjunction unit with the single-complex sections augmentation by the derived adjunction unit formula. Set λ=asIso(θ) followed by the inverse of RΓ(asIso(e)); d.counit_iso supplies this last isomorphism. Its inverse identity gives λ.hom ≫ RΓ(e)=θ. This construction needs no nonzero generator choice, including A=0 and N=1.
